page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-112 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 112 vCPUs mapped to 56 physical cores with multithreading enabled, providing dedicated CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 224 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes L1d, L2, and L3 caches of 32 KB, 0.5 MB, and 32 MB respectively. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 164,157.35 and a PassMark CPU score of 94,729.97, both placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached reads reaching 7,743.98 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 274.99 GB/sec. Single-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2,924.97, while cryptographic operations perform exceptionally well, scoring 131,150.33 in PassMark encryption tests.

From a resource density perspective, the c2d-highcpu-112 offers high compute density relative to its memory footprint. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory arrays. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, limiting its utility for tasks requiring high-speed local disk I/O or hardware-accelerated parallel processing.

This server configuration is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput web serving. It is also well-suited for database operations and Redis deployments, supported by a Redis SET throughput of 121.03 million operations per second. While it can handle basic LLM inference, its text generation speeds remain average, making it better suited for CPU-based batch processing and parallelized computational tasks.
